title: Announce the rename and redesign (news post, Substack, partners)
description:
Write and send a short announcement of the rename and redesign. The changelog entry (changelog/2026-09-19-conscious-communities-redesign.md, flagged promote: true) is the factual base; the announcement is the human version and is a copy job, so Rufus writes and Claude edits (see the copy pass bead).

Pieces: 1) a news post on the site (blog/), in the voice of the July post "A new home for Developmental Spaces" (blog/a-new-home-for-developmental-spaces.md, 2026-07-15) which is now partly out of date (it describes the parchment look and the Developmental Spaces masthead). Leave that post as a record but add a one-line note at its top linking to the new post. 2) Substack post to the newsletter list. 3) Optional social. 4) Use the before and after screenshots already in changelog/images/.

Content to cover: why the name changed (Developmental Spaces is a mouthful and reads academic; Conscious Communities is what people say; the concept, whitepaper, manifesto and network keep the Developmental Spaces name), what the new look is and why (watercolour, Life Itself's own illustration), what is unchanged (all addresses, courses, archive, wiki), what is next. Do this after the rollout bead's domain and newsletter steps so links and names are consistent.

title: Roll out the rename beyond the site: domain, newsletter, email, partners
description:
The site is live as Conscious Communities but the rest of the world still says Developmental Spaces. Do these, in roughly this order. Reasoning and rules of use are in docs/branding/naming.md (section "Rules of use" and "Open items").

1. Domain: consciouscommunities.net is Rufus's (registered on Cloudflare 2026-01-03). Point it at developmentalspaces.org with a 301 redirect (Cloudflare redirect rule). consciouscommunities.org is parked for sale on Afternic and .com is taken; buying the .org is a Rufus decision, not assumed. consciouscollectives.org is also Rufus's and stays unused ("communities" is the better word). Keep developmentalspaces.org as the canonical domain; do not move it.
2. Newsletter: Substack (developmentalspaces.substack.com) display name to Conscious Communities; the URL stays. Check the About/description text there.
3. Email: the mailer repo (../devspaces-mailer, github life-itself/devspaces-mailer) still says "Developmental Spaces" in the subscribe confirmation page (src/index.js, link text, old cream palette #faf6ec / #2a2118) and in every email footer ("Developmental Spaces · Life Itself"). Change the visible name and restyle the confirmation page to the new look (near-white, ink, yellow, PT Serif). Do NOT change the sending address courses@mail.developmentalspaces.org or the DNS; the deliverability stack (SPF, DKIM, DMARC, plain-text part) was hard-won and works.
4. Partners: send a short note to Fetzer, Commonweal, Ekskaret, Springboard and LIONE that the public name is now Conscious Communities and why (two paragraphs from naming.md are enough). Ask Life Itself to update links and descriptions that say "Developmental Spaces initiative" (lifeitself.org posts such as building-field-for-developmental-spaces; the Life Itself site's own pages about this project).
5. Small places: GitHub repo description (currently "Manifesto website for developmental spaces and conscious coliving in an age between worlds."), Google Analytics property name (G-CN5D9D57PC), any social handles, email signature lines.
6. Social/OG: add an Open Graph image and check page titles and descriptions for the main pages (a card built from the road painting and the yellow block would do). Confirm the favicon shows in tabs.

Acceptance: searching the web and following old links lands people on a consistent Conscious Communities presence; nothing user-facing says only "Developmental Spaces" where it should say the public name, except the concept, paper, manifesto and network. The July blog post (blog/a-new-home-for-developmental-spaces.md) stays as a historical record.

title: Redesign follow-ups (Conscious Communities, direction E)
description:
Follow-up work after the Conscious Communities rename and the direction E (watercolour) redesign went live on 2026-09-19 (merge 2f80f16 on main; changelog entry changelog/2026-09-19-conscious-communities-redesign.md). Start a new session by reading AGENTS.md, then docs/branding/README.md (current state, links, decision log), then docs/branding/design-direction.md section 7 (the design rules in force).

STATE. Live in production: home, Learn, Build, Fund, Find, About, whitepaper and manifesto openers, the painted catalogue at the top of /what, restyled course signup forms. Site name is Conscious Communities; Developmental Spaces stays the name of the concept, whitepaper, manifesto and network (docs/branding/naming.md). Design: near-white page, PT Serif set tight, Source Sans 3, one yellow (#FFD23F), watercolour illustration, no photographs on the front door. All paintings are STAND-INS borrowed from the Awami Conscious Food book. The spiral mark is generated in code.

DECIDED (do not relitigate without Rufus): direction E over A to D; no photography commission; the site is about the general idea, not the Bergerac hub; illustration carries ideas and photographs only appear as captioned documentary plates on pages about actual places; Samarra etching is good but belongs inside as a plate, not on a cover; copy is a separate human job; naming decision is not to be revisited until six months after go-live (see the deferred review bead).

SUGGESTED ORDER. 1) rename rollout and announcement (the site is already live under the new name, so the rest of the world is now inconsistent); 2) copy pass (Rufus writes, Claude edits); 3) /what rebuild; 4) remaining interior pages; 5) QA pass; 6) illustrations, then whitepaper cover and diagram, which depend on them; 7) housekeeping.

WORKING NOTES. Preview with `fl . --yes` (site ds-redesign-preview). The preview skips the build/ folder, lags on custom.css by 10 to 20 minutes, and ignores contentExclude; AGENTS.md has the workarounds. Pushing to main deploys to production within about a minute. docs/ is excluded from the site but visible on the public GitHub repo. The two Claude artifacts (mood board, home mockups) are linked in docs/branding/README.md with their source saved in docs/branding/moodboard-artifact/ and docs/branding/mockups/.

title: New illustrations to replace the Awami stand-ins (and check rights)
description:
Every painting on the live site is borrowed from the Awami Conscious Food System book (Life Itself, 2026; illustrated by Jennifer Chan, who is no longer around; Valerie Duvauchelle author). They are stand-ins. Replace or supplement them with a set of our own in the same language.

STEP 0, do first: confirm with Rufus (a) whether the Awami book is released and (b) that using Jennifer Chan's paintings publicly is fine beyond the launch. The About page already credits her and the book by name, and the GitHub repo is PUBLIC, so nothing from the book beyond the cut-out paintings already on the site should be committed (the full PDF sits in the git-ignored sandbox/ folder of Rufus's checkout, and page renders were deliberately left out of docs/branding/moodboard-artifact/). Also locate the original Canva source so figures can be re-extracted at full resolution; the PDF extraction (pdfimages, about 50 paintings, each with an alpha mask) gave cut-outs up to about 2500px, and assets/illustrations/ holds them downsized to 1100px WebP.

STYLE RULES to match: loose watercolour on transparent cut-outs; figures doing something, not posing; one flat yellow (#FFD23F) as the only flat colour; no text inside images; no photographic realism; abstract washes and ribbons are fine; descriptive alt text in the markup.

WHAT IS NEEDED (roughly in priority): 1) a drawn spiral mark to replace the generated brushed one (nav logo assets/cc-spiral.png and favicon assets/cc-favicon.png); 2) a circle of people; 3) a house with many doors; 4) the five domains, drawn (the current diagram assets/paper/domains-5.png is a hand-drawn Integral-style set of circles with emoji); 5) the three streams (Learn, Build, Fund) as three distinct small paintings; 6) a new whitepaper cover in the same hand, keeping the double-circle spiral idea, not Samarra (see the whitepaper bead); 7) a Samarra plate treatment for use inside pages (the etching assets/tower.png is good, only too much for a cover).

SUPPLY OPTIONS in order: 1) reuse the Awami paintings (current state); 2) procedural washes and shapes in code (canvas): the generator for the washes, the cover mock and the brushed spiral is inside docs/branding/mockups/2026-09-18-home-direction-e.html, good for backgrounds and marks, not for figures; 3) an image model (Midjourney, Flux or similar) with Awami paintings as style references: Claude can write the prompts and style sheet, Rufus curates hard, because uncurated output drifts into generic AI watercolour, the exact thing this design avoids; 4) commission a small set (about ten pieces would carry the site).

Acceptance: every painting on the site is either cleared for use or replaced; the mark, favicon and cover are drawn rather than generated; assets/illustrations/ holds the set with a short README of provenance and rights.

title: QA pass: dark mode, mobile, accessibility, performance, links
description:
A QA pass over the live site, then fix what it finds.

1) Dark mode: config.json / custom.css define Flowershow dark tokens (--color-d-*), but the cc-* components use fixed light colours (--cc-page, --cc-ink, yellow blocks, transparent cut-out paintings on a light ground). Check what a visitor with a dark OS setting sees. Either implement a proper dark palette (paintings on dark will look wrong; multiply blend on the yellow sections will not work) or force light mode.
2) Mobile (400px) on every page and tablet (768px): hero painting size, list rows, the yellow sections, nav and search, the newsletter form.
3) Accessibility: keyboard focus states on .cc-list links, buttons and the form (the form has one; check the rest); colour contrast of --cc-mute (#6A6A66) on #F5F5F3 and on yellow (#5a4a00 labels on #FFD23F); heading order (the designed pages use one h1 then h2/h3); meaningful alt text for every painting; link text that makes sense out of context ("Read the full argument" is fine, check for bare "Start here").
4) Performance: paintings in assets/illustrations total about 1.1 MB; the whitepaper cover assets/paper/ds-paper-cover-2025.jpg is 1.4 MB and is used at 13rem wide, so resize it; fonts load through @import in custom.css (render-blocking), so consider preconnect or a head tag in config.json; run Lighthouse on home and one stream.
5) Cross-browser: Safari and Firefox (the pages use :has(), mix-blend-mode, clamp()).
6) Broken links: run a link check over the site, especially pages that pointed at anchors or classes that changed; /paper#executive-summary anchor from the home page must land on the summary heading.

title: Redesign the remaining interior pages, then delete the legacy ds-* CSS
description:
Only the home, Learn, Build, Fund, Find, About, the whitepaper and manifesto openers and the top of /what are properly redesigned. Everything else renders through custom.css (fonts, colours, yellow link underlines, ds-* legacy classes restyled) and works, but is plain prose in the Flowershow default layout with the file-tree sidebar and contents column.

TO DO: decide a template for each family and apply it. Families: 1) wiki (about 65 notes plus index; probably keep as reading pages but check the sidebar and tables); 2) blog index and posts (blog/index.md, the July post uses screenshots of the old design); 3) network, why, resources, examples list (examples.md uses a Flowershow <List> component with image, headline, eyebrow slots; see also the exemplars bead); 4) course pages: learn/courses/*/index.md and the ~27 lesson pages, learn/reading.md, learn/what-is-conscious-coliving.md; a hero painting on each course index would help; 5) build/vision.md, fund/the-fund-we-almost-built.md and the fund/archive pages (sober register, tables); 6) the 404 page.

CHECKS: in production (not the preview, which ignores contentExclude) confirm the left sidebar on prose pages does not list docs, .beads or other excluded folders, and decide whether to hide the sidebar site-wide with showSidebar: false and rely on the nav plus in-page contents. Confirm search still works and its highlight is yellow.

CLEAN-UP when done: search for remaining class="ds-..." in the markdown and migrate them, then delete the legacy ds-* block at the bottom of custom.css. Follow the patterns in index.md and learn/index.md (cc-page, hero hero-sm, cc-list, cc-yellow). Look at every page at 1440px and 400px.

title: Rebuild /what as a designed catalogue page aligned with the whitepaper
description:
/what is currently the old Flowershow markdown page with the painted catalogue (mockup 3) bolted on top and the old definition text beneath. Rebuild it as a designed page in the catalogue style AND bring its content in line with the whitepaper.

DESIGN: use layout: plain with the cc-page components (see index.md, learn/index.md and docs/branding/mockups/2026-09-18-home-direction-e.html mockup 3 "The catalogue"): yellow block opener, tight title, the eight-item catalogue of painted things a developmental space is made of (shared table, house, rhythm, roles that rotate, practices, circle, land and food, energy: labels are placeholders), then sections. Paintings are stand-ins (see the illustrations bead).

CONTENT: restructure around the whitepaper's executive summary (paper.md, "Executive Summary"): 1) the definition: "Dedicated, growth-oriented spaces where communities engage in sustained, multi-domain inner development in the service of socio-cultural transformation"; 2) the five domains of inner development with the paper's names (Waking up, Cognitive development, Growing up, Cleaning up, Showing up), plus the caution about growth hierarchies and "maps and rafts"; 3) why now (metacrisis, resilience and flourishing); 4) why dedicated spaces (containment, community, continuity: state to trait, communities of purpose, emotional safety, generative social fields, pockets of change); 5) the characteristics (core 5.1 and flexible 5.2). The existing text (Preface: centres more than boundaries; Outlines from July 2024, Nov 2021, 2020) moves to an appendix at the bottom or into the wiki; keep it, do not delete. Note the home page's domain list uses different names from the paper; reconcile (see the whitepaper bead).

Words on this page are mostly the authors' own (the paper); the lede and catalogue labels are copy and belong to the copy pass.

title: Copy pass: hero, tagline, three door sentences, stream heroes
description:
Design went first; the words are a separate, human job. Rufus writes, Claude edits (do not rewrite copy unasked). Current text on the live site is PLACEHOLDER copy that avoids the worst problems but is not final.

KNOWN PROBLEMS (from the mood board artifact's copy section, https://claude.ai/artifact/7RkR5Dg45Jn9JNtTA55nMj, and docs/branding/moodboard.md): 1) an earlier draft repeated "people grow" in the eyebrow and the headline, and asked the reader to accept "developmental space" before it was explained; 2) a lede that lists formats (co-living houses, retreat centres, monastery, university) before saying what they have in common: the common thing should come first; 3) "exploring them, building them and funding them" is the site's structure showing through: a visitor needs to feel addressed before being routed; 4) stream names and subtitles explain the site instead of speaking to someone.

CURRENT PLACEHOLDERS on the home page (index.md): h1 "Communities where people grow." sub "the home of developmental spaces"; lede "Some communities exist so that the people in them can grow: ..."; buttons "Start with a free course", "Read the whitepaper"; door sentences for Learn ("living together, on purpose"), Build ("spaces that grow people"), Fund ("land, stewardship, capital"). The chosen tagline in docs/branding/naming.md is "Developmental spaces where people grow." and is used in the footer and meta description, but the hero uses "the home of developmental spaces": reconcile.

SCOPE: hero (h1, sub, lede, CTA labels); the three door sentences; the stream heroes and subtitles (Learn, Build, Fund, Find, About); the yellow-section statements on each stream page; the About page's "Two names" paragraph; the domain names on the home page vs the whitepaper (see the whitepaper bead); meta descriptions and the positioning line ("the home of the developmental spaces field", brand-narrative.md). VOICE per stream (docs/branding/brand-narrative.md): home and Learn plain, warm, concrete; Build visionary and rigorous, one click deep; Fund sober and finance-literate; never salesy, never vague. Two-beat visitor experience: "this is the kind of community I want to live in" then "oh, there is serious design thinking here."

Suggested process: one working session, Rufus drafts hero and door sentences aloud or in a doc, Claude tightens against the voice rules and checks length in the layout at 1440px and 400px.

title: Migrate ratified consolidation decisions and analysis into internal docs
description:
Migrate ratified consolidation decisions and analysis into internal docs (docs/, excluded from the published site).

DONE 2026-09-18/19: docs/branding/ now holds the naming decision (naming.md), the brand narrative migrated and revised (brand-narrative.md), the design direction and identity history (design-direction.md), the mood board notes and artifact source (moodboard.md, moodboard-artifact/), the home mockups (mockups/), a README with current state, links and decision log. The sibling folder's brand-narrative.md carries a "moved" note pointing here (uncommitted edit in that repo, see below).

REMAINING in ../devspaces-consolidation (a separate git repo): BRIEF.md (mission, job stories per stream, voice and register), sitemap.md (information architecture), motivation.md, PLAN.md, BACKLOG.md, NOTES-manual-actions.md, and the ref/ folder. Migrate BRIEF, sitemap and motivation into docs/ as they are the durable strategy; PLAN, BACKLOG and NOTES are project management and can stay. Close out PLAN.md Phase 2 (redesign) by linking to docs/branding/README.md, mark HANDOFF-design.md as superseded (it says to start from the June exploration and warm monastic), and commit the one-line "moved" note in brand-narrative.md that is currently uncommitted there.

DO NOT migrate ref/2026-02-11-whatsapp-consolidation-responses.md, the ChatGPT naming thread, or the WhatsApp screenshots into this public repo; they name private group participants. See also the privacy bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- `docs/` contains a clear, discoverable decision/strategy record for this project.
- It captures at minimum: the Developmental Spaces umbrella name and public-language doctrine; ratified tagline and its status; mission/positioning; primary and secondary audiences; Learn/Build/Fund job stories and IA; voice/register; and any relevant brand design direction.
- Each entry identifies its source file and decision date/status, and distinguishes locked decisions from open items.
- Relevant reasoning/analysis is retained or linked so future contributors can understand why choices were made.
- A review compares the inventory against `../devspaces-consolidation` and records intentional omissions.

title: Exclude internal docs from Flower Show publishing
description:
Configure this repository so the top-level `docs/` directory is excluded from Flower Show’s published content while remaining tracked in Git.

Context: the repository needs a private-to-the-site documentation area for strategy, decisions, and implementation notes. Flower Show should not generate routes or navigation entries from files under `docs/`.

Implementation notes:
- Identify and use Flower Show’s supported ignore/exclusion mechanism (rather than relying only on navigation omission).
- Keep existing publishable Markdown content outside `docs/` unaffected.
- Document the convention briefly so future internal documentation is placed under `docs/`.
acceptance_criteria:
- A representative Markdown file under `docs/` produces no published Flower Show page.
- Existing public pages continue to build and publish normally.
- The exclusion is committed as repository configuration and the `docs/` convention is documented.
close_reason: Done 2026-09-19: contentExclude now lists /docs, /.beads, /sandbox, /README, /AGENTS, /CLAUDE in config.json. Verified in production: /docs, /docs/branding, /.beads, /sandbox all return 404.

title: Exemplars and Find: documentary plates, real photographs, consistent list
description:
Design rule from docs/branding/design-direction.md section 7: illustration carries ideas; photographs carry evidence, and only on pages about actual places, as captioned documentary plates (uniform size, place and year in the caption, never full-bleed, never the hero). The exemplars (/examples, /find) are exactly those pages and are not yet done.

FOUND: many images in assets/ that look like place photos (plum-village.jpg, tamera.png, sieben-linden.png, embercombe1.jpg, monasticacademy.jpg, omega-institute.jpg and others) are actually screenshots of those organisations' websites, taken for the examples pages, so they are not usable as photography and have inconsistent aspect ratios and quality.

TO DO: for each example, a real photograph (with permission or clear licence, credited) or a painted/drawn placeholder; one uniform plate size; caption with name, place and year; consistent list layout for /examples (currently a Flowershow <List> component with image, headline and eyebrow slots, see examples.md) and a detail page per example if useful; keep the "very partial list created in 2023" note honest. Also decide how to invite submissions (Google form link exists in examples.md). Do not use photographs of the Life Itself hub as a stand-in for the idea; this site is about the general idea, not one house.

title: Whitepaper design: new cover, redrawn five domains, PDF and page layout
description:
Rufus wants the whitepaper itself (not only its web page) to be more beautiful and in line with the new identity; the cover and diagrams can change freely. Depends on the illustrations bead for new artwork, but the layout thinking can start now.

SCOPE: 1) a new cover: keep the double-circle spiral idea (there is something about it), drop Samarra from the cover (good etching, too much for a cover), straw-yellow paper is no longer the palette, so decide between the near-white page with one yellow block and painted spirals, as in the Awami cover pattern (wash, flat yellow square, tight title); 2) redraw the five domains diagram (assets/paper/domains-5.png: circles labelled Waking up, Cognitive, Growing up, Cleaning up, Showing up, with emoji) as a painting or a clean drawing in the new hand; 3) re-lay the PDF (full paper and executive summary; the Google Drive links are in paper.md): typography (PT Serif tight titles, Source Sans 3 for captions and tables), chapter openers in the style of the Awami book, yellow blocks used sparingly; 4) the web page /paper: consider splitting the executive summary and the full text into reading pages with the severe register (type only, one yellow block), currently the summary sits on one long page under the designed opener; 5) reconcile the names of the five domains between the paper (Waking up, Cognitive development, Growing up, Cleaning up, Showing up) and the home page list (Cognitive development, Awakening, Healing, Evolving worldview, Engaged action). Rufus/authors decide which set is canonical; the home page should match the paper. The authors are Rosie Bell, Boaz Feldman, Rufus Pollock (Sep 2025); changing the paper's cover or text is theirs to approve.

title: Review the naming decision six months after go-live (on or after 2027-03-19)
description: The ratified doctrine (docs/branding/brand-narrative.md, docs/branding/naming.md) says not to relitigate the name before the redesign has been live for six months. The masthead flip went live on 2026-09-19, so review on or after 2027-03-19. Questions then: did the public name help the primary audience (people exploring conscious community living)? Is Developmental Spaces still right for the concept and the paper? Are the two names being used consistently? Cheapest things to change first: tagline, then hero words, then masthead. Look at analytics (G-CN5D9D57PC), newsletter signups, and any feedback from the network.

title: Flowershow tooling: fl skips build/, preview cache lag, changelog listing
description:
Tooling notes worth turning into fixes or upstream reports; none blocks the site.

1) The `fl` CLI (v2.2.0; 2.3.0 available) never publishes a folder named `build`, so /build cannot be previewed; workaround in AGENTS.md (temporary top-level copy). Report to the Flowershow maintainers or rename nothing. 2) The preview site serves custom.css from an edge cache that can lag 10 to 20 minutes after `fl . --yes` even though the response says cache-control max-age=0 and reports "in sync"; workaround is comparing md5 of the local file with the served one. 3) The preview ignores contentExclude, production enforces it; docs/ therefore appears in the preview. 4) `.flowershow` (committed) names the preview site "ds-redesign-preview"; consider a neutral name such as developmentalspaces-preview and delete the old preview site with `fl delete`.
5) Add "changelog/" listing: the changelog convention (life-itself/changelog) anticipates a Flowershow listing page built from changelog/*.md frontmatter; entries are currently reachable only by URL (for example /changelog/2026-09-19-conscious-communities-redesign). Decide whether to add an index page or exclude the folder from the site.
notes: 2026-09-19 finding: in production contentExclude hid docs/, .beads/ and sandbox/ (pages and raw files) but served the raw AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md until the filename forms 'AGENTS.md' and 'CLAUDE.md' were added next to '/AGENTS' and '/CLAUDE'; the pages briefly returned 500 before settling to 404. The preview (fl) publishes docs/ and .beads/config.yaml; it did NOT publish the 150MB sandbox PDF (raw URL 404).
